steps.description: Filter low-abundance genes: compute the mean log2 expression per gene and set a floor at the low end of the distribution (state the numeric floor chosen), keeping a gene when it is above the floor in at least 6 samples — the smallest group size. The floor must be chosen from the overall expression distribution, independent of the condition labels. Report the number of genes kept out of 12000. Do NOT normalize again: the facility already normalized these values, and a second normalization would hide what they did; instead record the observed value range and state the scale (log2(TPM+1)) in the outputs. Build the design as ~0 + condition on the aligned metadata with the factor levels set explicitly so that control is the reference, and define the contrast as treated - control, so a positive log2FC means higher expression in treated. Fit with lmFit, apply the contrast, and call eBayes with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE. plan.title: Treated vs control DE on log2 expression (limma-trend)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12000 x 13 CSV of log2(TPM+1) values from the core facility (log_expr.csv, first column = gene id, 12 sample columns) plus a 12 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv: sample, condition) describing 6 treated vs 6 control human muscle samples, unpaired, single batch. Because the delivered matrix holds normalized log2 values and NOT counts, the negative-binomial pipelines (DESeq2, edgeR, voom) are inapplicable — they require raw integer counts and back-converting log2(TPM+1) to pseudo-counts would fabricate a count distribution. The plan therefore uses limma with an intensity-dependent trend in the empirical Bayes step (limma-trend) with robust hyperparameter estimation, which is the method of record for log-scale abundance data.

T1S1 establishes sample structure before any model is fitted: value-range check to confirm the matrix really is log2 scale (roughly 0-20, fractional) rather than a mislabeled count table, PCA/MDS on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and per-sample detected-gene counts, all coloured by condition. This is where an outlier or an unlabeled processing split would surface; with n=6 per group a single outlier materially moves the result, so the step reports rather than silently drops.

T1S2 filters low-abundance genes on mean log expression with a floor set independently of the group labels (a gene must clear the floor in at least 6 samples, the smallest group size), does NOT re-normalize, fits ~0 + condition with an explicit contrast treated - control so that a positive log2FC means higher in treated, runs eBayes(trend=TRUE, robust=TRUE), and takes results with topTable(adjust.method="BH"). A fold-change-thresholded result is produced with treat() rather than a post-hoc filter on the estimate, so the FDR control applies to the threshold question actually asked.

T1S3 assembles the report: method, package versions, design and contrast, thresholds, number of genes tested after filtering, number of DE genes, volcano and top-gene heatmap, and the full sessionInfo reproducibility record. With 6 vs 6 the study is modestly powered; the report states the tested-gene count and the significant count together and does not present a nominal-p list as a finding.

No enrichment step is planned — the research question asks only which genes differ, and pathway analysis would be unasked scope.

Low abundance filter on log2 expression values
~0 + condition with explicit reference level control
limma linear model on log-scale expression values (limma-trend)
topTable BH adjustment; TREAT against a stated lfc threshold
Method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, sessionInfo
